clue.text: Flies national leader around capital

indicators.note: around tells us the leader's name is wrapped about the city's name

parts.note: Moses led the Israelite nation out of Egypt
Quito is the capital city of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A head of state is circling the capital in a light aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' reads as a verb about the leader, but it is the noun definition. The plural with -ES is the spelling the wordplay forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosquitoes are small biting insects, a family of true flies.

clue.text: Author article bringing unexpected benefit

parts.note: Thomas Mann was the German novelist of The Magic Mountain
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer's magazine piece brings in an unlooked-for windfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, the food from heaven of Exodus is any windfall or boon arriving unexpectedly.

clue.text: Smile more falsely as part of restaurant staff

indicators.note: a smile put on falsely is faked, so these letters are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A waiter is told to put on a broader fake grin for the diners.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter is an employee of a restaurant who advises on and serves the wine.

clue.text: Not good enough, as units damaged workplace

indicators.note: damaged units are broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a factory is a place where people work making goods

explanation.surface: A quality inspector condemns a plant whose units arrived damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns AS UNITS into UNSATIS, followed by FACTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that falls short of an acceptable standard is inadequate, a plain synonym.

clue.text: River bottom as place for experimental trials

parts.note: the Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout
a bed is the bottom of a river or sea

explanation.surface: A riverbed is being used as a site for scientific experiments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a river in southern England, a favourite in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig or setting where new equipment or ideas are tried out is a proving ground for trials.

clue.text: Producers of some pictures, and so on, belonging to female

parts.note: etc is the abbreviation for et cetera, meaning and so on
hers is the possessive meaning belonging to her

explanation.surface: A list of artists and their works ends with a note that one painting is a woman's.
explanation.definitionFit: Printmakers who bite designs into metal plates with acid make one kind of picture.

clue.text: Something worn in Amritsar, India

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of the city name and country

explanation.surface: A tourist note about what people wear in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The city and country name look like the setting, but they are where the garment's letters sit, across 'Amritsar' and 'India'.
explanation.definitionFit: The draped garment of Indian women is a classic item of clothing, exactly what one would see worn.

clue.text: A couple of bishops with sacred books for monastic leader

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, and two of them give BB
OT is the Old Testament, the sacred books of the Hebrew Bible

explanation.surface: A pair of bishops bring scripture to the head of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an abbey of monks is its superior, the monastery's leader.

clue.text: Cross religious group put in ground initially

indicators.note: initially says the burial word comes at the start, before the group

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body in the ground
a sect is a breakaway religious group

explanation.surface: An angry religious group buries someone at the start of a ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective angry but is the verb meaning to meet across.
explanation.definitionFit: Two lines that pass through each other cross; to meet and cut across is the verb sense.

clue.text: Knowing another's mind, however, and putting one's foot down

parts.note: though can mean however, as in 'he did go, though'
treading is stepping, literally setting a foot down

explanation.surface: Someone senses what a partner thinks, yet still insists firmly on their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting one's foot down' suggests being firm, but here it is literal stepping.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy, discerning someone else's unspoken thoughts, is mind-reading.

clue.text: Greek goddess in scattered Meissen collection

indicators.note: scattered pieces of porcelain are spread about, so these letters are rearranged; 'collection' adds to the same signal

explanation.surface: A goddess figurine sits among a jumbled collection of German porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: Meissen is a German porcelain town. 'scattered' and 'collection' both say the letters are gathered into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of retribution punished arrogance, giving her name to any downfall.

clue.text: Share a property with a lot of salmon? Somewhat

indicators.note: a lot of the fish's name, but not all of it, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the coho is a Pacific salmon
a bit means somewhat, as in 'a bit tired'

explanation.surface: An estate agent's pitch: a house to share with a fair quantity of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' suggests real estate, but it means the home two partners share.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who live together without marrying set up home jointly under one roof.

clue.text: State organized data collection? That's not bound to happen

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
a table sets out data in ordered rows and columns

explanation.surface: A government database is questioned as to whether it is inevitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation, but it is the verb to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be prevented or warded off is not inevitable, so it need not occur.

clue.text: Speak without any qualification

definitions.meaning: to say or voice words aloud
complete or absolute, as in 'total nonsense'

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to voice words; the adjective means absolute, without reservation.

clue.text: Tell, for example, leaders of striking workers if stoppage's suspended

indicators.note: the leaders of each of these words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Union bosses tell striking workers what happens if the walkout is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb, but it is William Tell, the legendary archer hero of Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell, legendary hero of Switzerland, is one instance of a person from that country.

clue.text: Security device the point of which isn't clear when it works

definitions.text: Security device the point of which isn't clear when it works

parts.words: Security device the point of which isn't clear when it works
parts.note: a fastener whose sharp tip is hidden in a guard when closed, so its point is not visible while it is doing its job

explanation.walkthrough: 'point' plays on purpose versus a sharp tip, and 'security' on safety rather than guarding property.
explanation.definitionFit: The bent fastener with its tip held in a clasp is a small device securing fabric safely.

clue.text: Release Duke, having mistreated his grace

indicators.note: words mistreated are knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman is freed after he has abused a bishop addressed as His Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His Grace' is the form of address for a duke or archbishop, which makes the surface plausible; here the two words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go or set free, as a patient from hospital, is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Discovering minister with part of our capital

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion
Ealing is a borough of London, the British setter's own capital

explanation.surface: Someone finds a clergyman living in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a borough in west London; 'our capital' assumes a British solver.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective-like participle, disclosing or uncovering something is laying it bare.

clue.text: Prepared in advance and arranged around organ

indicators.note: around says the word for arranged is wrapped about the organ

parts.note: formed means shaped or arranged, as troops are formed up
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A musician sets up ahead of time by placing chairs around the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb 'forewarned is forearmed': ready ahead of trouble, already equipped.

clue.text: Organized criminals, if I am so bad

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoilt, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession: gangsters are convinced the speaker is truly wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns IF I AM SO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Sicilian-American crime syndicate are the classic organized gangsters.

clue.text: For these heavy sleepers, clean room kept in reserve?

parts.note: to do a room is to clean it, as in 'do the bathroom'
ice is cool reserve of manner, as in an icy reserve

explanation.surface: A hotel holds a freshly cleaned room back for guests who sleep long and deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' joins the pieces; 'clean room' tempts as a laboratory, but it is DO plus RM.
explanation.definitionFit: These small rodents famously hibernate for months, the Alice dormouse forever nodding off.

clue.text: Split, with little time to join together

parts.note: to rive is an old word for to split or tear apart
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A torn item needs a moment's work to be fixed together again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' and 'join together' pull opposite ways, one piece and one definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten metal plates with a headed pin is to fix them together firmly.

clue.text: Warm temperature in front of kiln

indicators.note: in front of places the temperature letter before the kiln

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent, England

explanation.surface: Someone stands by a kiln to warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a kiln building for drying hops in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat by a fire, as one warms hands or bread, is a synonym.

clue.text: Shining silver base

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
low and base both mean mean or contemptible

explanation.surface: A description of a gleaming silver stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing with light or colour, something radiant and bright is gleaming.

clue.text: Frame badly and hang crookedly in part of Ireland

indicators.note: framed badly, the word's letters are jumbled
hung crookedly, the word's letters are put askew in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone makes a poor job of framing and hanging a picture of an Irish scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'badly' makes FERMA from FRAME, 'crookedly' makes NAGH from HANG. It is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, so geographically a region of the island.

clue.text: Likely to sink, and did sink?

definitions.meaning: a ship pierced below the waterline is going to go down
a golfer who putts the ball into the cup has sunk it

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is golf: to hole a putt is to sink it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hull with a hole punched in it is doomed; holing out in golf is sinking the putt.

clue.text: Friend abandoned Rome or another Italian city

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so these letters are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend leaves the capital for a different city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' seems to say the friend left Rome, but it is the signal turning ROME into ERMO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian capital is a city in Italy other than the one named in the clue.

clue.text: First write two or three letters, usually

definitions.meaning: coming at the very beginning, as an opening letter

definitions.text: write two or three letters, usually
definitions.meaning: to sign a document with the first letters of one's names, typically two or three

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means earliest; the verb means to mark a document with one's abbreviated signature.

clue.text: Creature that's supposedly drunk, but not always legless

definitions.text: Creature that's supposedly drunk, but not always legless

parts.words: Creature that's supposedly drunk, but not always legless
parts.note: British slang has the very drunk as 'pissed as a' this amphibian; 'legless' means drunk, yet these creatures have legs except as tadpoles

explanation.walkthrough: 'legless' is British slang for very drunk, but read literally it is the tadpole stage before legs grow.
explanation.definitionFit: This small amphibian is the one in the British simile for drunkenness and grows legs after its tadpole stage.

clue.text: Unattached daughter is English and no longer young

parts.note: aged means old, no longer young

explanation.surface: A single English daughter is getting on in years.
explanation.definitionFit: Detached or not connected, as a gear freed from its mesh, is a plain synonym.
